profile.summary: A study that combines two saturation genome editing (SGE) screens of the BRCA2 DNA binding domain into four composite functional models, checks each against known pathogenic and benign variants, and then feeds the best one (the Integrated VarCall model) into ClinGen BRCA1/2 expert panel classification rules. It reports sensitivity and specificity against ClinVar and HDR assay standards, and the share of 6383 variants that could be classified. It is relevant to clinical variant scientists using BRCA2 functional data.

summary_quotes.text: we combined results from these studies in four composite models and evaluated the performance of each model using variants with known classifications

Thus, 92.8% (5926 of 6383) overall and 90.3% (4006 of 4438) of all missense variants were classified as P/LP or B/LB whereas only 12.2% (780 of 6383) of variants overall and 2.8% (126 of 4438) of missense variants were classified without incorporation of the functional results

sections.title: What it measures
sections.body: Two things. First, how accurately each functional model (two original SGE studies, a concordance model, an Integrated VarCall model, an Integrated GMM model and a secondary concordance model) separates known pathogenic from benign variants. Second, how many BRCA2 variants can be classified as pathogenic or benign once the best functional model's evidence is added to the ClinGen rules.

quotes.text: Results were compared to those from the two original studies
using established pathogenic and benign clinical standards from ClinVar and functional standards from a well-calibrated homology directed DNA repair (HDR) assay

sections.title: How it is built
sections.body: 6383 SNVs were scored in both SGE studies (HAP1 cells and humanised mouse ES cells); 1041 of them had discordant results. The Integrated VarCall model pools raw scores from both studies in a Bayesian hierarchical model with batch effects; silent variants are assumed benign and nonsense variants pathogenic, and the prior probability of pathogenicity is 0.2. Reference standards are 158 ClinVar P/LP and B/LB missense variants not influenced by SGE results and common to all six models, and 316 HDR assay missense standards.

sections.title: Evaluation methodology
sections.body: Because all models reach close to 100% when every pathogenic or benign category is counted, the comparison uses only the Pathogenic_Strong and Benign_Strong/Moderate categories: sensitivity against P/LP standards (or HDR abnormal) and specificity against B/LB standards (or HDR normal). The Integrated VarCall model reaches 98.9% sensitivity and 100% specificity on the ClinVar standards, and 97% and 100% on the HDR standards. Its functional calls are then combined with other evidence under ENIGMA specification version 1.2.0 and the classification yield is counted. A separate case-control analysis tests whether Pathogenic_Strong missense variants raise cancer risk: odds ratios from logistic regression adjusted for age and ancestry, 5.46 (95% CI 4.07 to 7.48) for breast cancer and 6.83 (95% CI 4.51 to 10.40) for ovarian cancer, using Ambry Genetics cases and AllofUs controls.

sections.title: How to run it
sections.body: The repository provides the VarCall analysis in R with JAGS. Clone it, install JAGS and the listed R packages, then run runRtex.R in the VarCall folder. This reproduces the functional probabilities, not the comparison against ClinVar and HDR standards, for which no script is described.

run_guide.summary: Reproduce the Integrated VarCall functional probabilities for the BRCA2 SGE variants.
prerequisites: R with the packages knitr, rjags, R2WinBUGS, R2jags and mgcv.
The README says the short run takes about one hour and the longer run about 4 days.

steps.title: Get the code
steps.explanation: The README's clone line ends in /VarCall/, which git cannot clone; the repository root is cloned instead, and a checkout line pins the reviewed commit.

quotes.text: git clone https://github.com/najiemayo/Couch_SGE_BRCA2_MAVE_Mayo_NCI_joint_analysis/VarCall/

steps.title: Install the R packages
steps.explanation: Install JAGS first. The README gives the install.packages line to type inside R; here it is wrapped in Rscript -e.

quotes.text: First install JAGS in the system following the link here: https://mcmc-jags.sourceforge.io/
install.packages(c("knitr", "rjags", "R2WinBUGS", "R2jags", "mgcv"))

steps.title: Run the VarCall model
steps.explanation: The README asks for the data files combined.raw.tsv, variant_type_for_train.csv and shyamBRCA2allCounts.txt in the VarCall folder; the repository tree at this commit already lists them there. Check that the working directory is where the script expects.

quotes.text: Download the full data files `combined.raw.tsv`, `variant_type_for_train.csv`, `shyamBRCA2allCounts.txt` and put them in the VarCall folder
In terminal, run R script. "Rscript runRtex.R"

outputs: MAVEpostProbs.csv, with the probability of being pathogenic (PrDel), log posterior odds, log Bayes factor and effect size with 95% bounds, plus diagnostic PDFs.
limitations: These commands were read from the repository and have not been executed by Rewire.
They reproduce functional probabilities only, not the sensitivity and specificity comparison or the ClinGen classification.
Results vary slightly between runs because the model is fitted by MCMC.
